description: Additional Advanced RPAS quiz questions generated 2026-10-01 with weak-topic emphasis.

questions.question: A multirotor is hovering in gusty wind near the edge of its published wind limit. Which control concern best explains why the pilot should keep a larger safety margin?
choices: A multirotor always becomes more stable as wind increases.
Only fixed-wing aircraft are affected by gust loading.
Wind affects video quality but not controllability.
The flight controller may need increasingly large control and power corrections, leaving less authority for a sudden gust or manoeuvre.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 theory-of-flight knowledge includes stability, control, and performance limits. Near a published limit, extra control margin matters because disturbances can consume remaining authority quickly.

exactRefs.objective: Explain aircraft stability, control, and performance effects relevant to RPAS operation.

questions.learningObjective: Apply stability and control concepts to decide whether wind conditions leave enough margin for safe RPAS control.

origin.request: Generate 50 Additional Questions for our Adv Drone Quiz

questions.question: A fixed-wing RPA launches with a heavier mapping payload than usual but the same wing and battery. What performance change should the pilot expect?
choices: No change unless the centre of gravity moves outside limits.
Only radio range changes.
Higher stall speed and reduced climb/endurance margin compared with the lighter configuration.
Lower stall speed because weight increases inertia.
questions.rationale: Increased weight raises the lift required for flight and generally increases stall speed while reducing climb and endurance margins.

exactRefs.objective: Describe how weight affects lift requirement and aircraft performance.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how increased operating weight affects stall speed, climb performance, and endurance.

questions.question: A quadcopter is descending vertically into its own disturbed downwash and becomes mushy despite adequate battery power. What aerodynamic issue is most relevant?
choices: The camera gimbal is absorbing lift.
The aircraft may be operating in recirculating/settling airflow where added power does not immediately restore normal lift.
The compass has reversed magnetic north.
A higher descent rate always improves rotor efficiency.
questions.rationale: Rotorcraft can lose lift effectiveness in disturbed descending airflow. The operational response is to recover with margin rather than relying only on added throttle.

exactRefs.objective: Identify rotorcraft aerodynamic conditions that affect control and lift.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize rotorcraft performance hazards during vertical descent and choose conservative recovery actions.

questions.question: A fixed-wing RPA is trimmed for normal cruise, but the pilot commands a steep bank to turn inside a small survey area. What must the pilot remember about stall margin?
choices: Banking increases load factor, so stall margin can decrease even if airspeed appears acceptable for level flight.
A banked turn lowers the load factor below one.
Stall margin is independent of manoeuvring.
Only multirotors can stall in turns.
questions.rationale: In a banked turn, the aircraft must produce more lift than in straight-and-level flight. That raises effective stall speed and reduces margin.

exactRefs.objective: Explain how manoeuvring affects stall speed and control margin.

questions.learningObjective: Apply load-factor concepts to fixed-wing RPA turn planning and stall avoidance.

questions.question: A pilot notices the RPA requires noticeably more power to hold altitude on a hot afternoon at a high-elevation site. Which explanation best connects theory of flight to the go/no-go decision?

Lower air density reduces aerodynamic and propulsion performance, so takeoff, climb, and endurance margins may be reduced.

exactRefs.objective: Assess density-altitude effects on anticipated launch and flight performance.
Explain performance effects caused by air density changes.

questions.learningObjective: Relate air density to RPA lift, propulsion, cooling, climb, and endurance performance.
